questions.questionText: Electromagnetic waves are produced by:
questions.solution: Accelerated charges radiate electromagnetic waves.

questions.questionText: The speed of electromagnetic waves in vacuum is:
questions.solution: c = 1/sqrt(mu0*e0) = 3 x 10^8 m/s.

questions.questionText: Which EM wave has the highest frequency?
questions.solution: Gamma rays have the highest frequency in the EM spectrum.

questions.questionText: Maxwell's displacement current is:
questions.solution: Displacement current Id = e0 * d(phi_E)/dt.

questions.questionText: In an EM wave E and B are:
questions.optionB: Perpendicular to each other and to propagation direction
questions.solution: E, B, and direction of propagation are mutually perpendicular.

questions.questionText: Which EM waves are used in RADAR?
questions.solution: Microwaves are used in RADAR systems.

questions.questionText: The ozone layer absorbs:
questions.solution: Ozone layer absorbs harmful UV radiation from the sun.

questions.questionText: Infrared radiation is used in:
questions.solution: IR radiation is emitted by warm bodies and used in night vision.

questions.questionText: X-rays are produced by:
questions.optionB: Deceleration of fast electrons hitting a target
questions.solution: X-rays are produced when high-speed electrons hit a metal target (Bremsstrahlung).

questions.questionText: The energy of an EM wave is:
questions.optionC: Equally shared between E and B fields
questions.solution: Energy is equally divided between electric and magnetic fields in an EM wave.

questions.questionText: EM waves carry:
questions.solution: EM waves transport both energy and momentum.

questions.questionText: The ratio E0/B0 in an EM wave equals:
questions.solution: E0/B0 = c (speed of light).

questions.questionText: EM waves are:
questions.solution: EM waves are transverse - E and B oscillate perpendicular to propagation.

questions.questionText: Which EM wave is used in TV remote controls?
questions.solution: TV remotes use infrared radiation.

questions.questionText: The wavelength range of visible light is approximately:
questions.solution: Visible light ranges from about 400 nm (violet) to 700 nm (red).

questions.questionText: Maxwell added which term to Ampere's law?
questions.solution: Maxwell added the displacement current e0*d(phi_E)/dt to Ampere's law.

questions.questionText: Greenhouse effect is caused by:
questions.optionB: Trapping of infrared radiation by atmospheric gases
questions.solution: Greenhouse gases trap infrared radiation re-radiated by Earth.

questions.questionText: Which EM wave has longest wavelength?
questions.solution: Radio waves have the longest wavelength.

questions.questionText: The intensity of an EM wave is proportional to:
questions.solution: Intensity I = (1/2)*e0*c*E0^2, proportional to E0^2.

questions.questionText: Microwaves have wavelength in the range:
questions.solution: Microwaves have wavelength approximately 1 mm to 30 cm.

questions.questionText: EM waves do not require:
questions.solution: EM waves can propagate through vacuum - no medium needed.

questions.questionText: The Poynting vector S represents:
questions.optionB: Rate of energy flow per unit area
questions.solution: Poynting vector S = E x B/mu0 gives energy flux (power per unit area).

questions.questionText: Which of the following can be polarized?
questions.solution: Only transverse waves (EM waves) can be polarized. Sound is longitudinal.

questions.questionText: UV rays are used for:
questions.solution: UV radiation kills bacteria and is used for sterilization.

questions.questionText: The dimension of 1/sqrt(mu0*e0) is:
questions.solution: 1/sqrt(mu0*e0) = c which has dimensions of velocity [LT^-1].
